rationale: Releasing local work on the quorum-arithmetic Candidate 0922502bc12a4af68ee74cb77942fd72 at the run's time boundary. The question is grounded and partly narrowed but not resolved: for even N, FastQuorumSize = F+(F+1)/2 and SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2 stop describing intersecting sets and a majority (N=4 gives 2 and 2), no captured file validates that N is odd (run.go:30 computes f = (N-1)/2 with no parity check), and handlePrepareReply rebuilds once it has SlowQuorumSize replies including its own (epaxos/epaxos.go:1210-1218). The remaining hazard was narrowed to a precondition rather than a size argument: a conflicting recovery needs a replica that reached the instance without recording its Commit, because handleCommit records COMMITTED for every receiver and startRecoveryForInstance returns early for a COMMITTED instance with commands (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1135), while bcastCommit skips non-Alive peers. That precondition belongs to membership/liveness (A4), which was not read, so the candidate is released with its premises recorded rather than escalated to an obligation or an invented claim. Nothing here asserts that even N is deployable or that the hazard occurs. This is a scoped stop of one candidate, not of the run: the confirmed durability finding (CLM-DURABLE-BAL, violated, confirmed) and the explained items remain as they are.
resume_conditions: Read the membership/liveness activity (A4): master registration, Alive transitions and reconnect handling, to determine whether a replica can advance crtInstance for a row while being skipped by the Commit broadcast.
Determine whether N parity is enforced outside the captured files (deployment tooling), since the code does not reject even N.
Read handlePrepareReply's restart-with-NOOP branch together with the Accept majority requirement (acceptOKs+1 > N/2) for N=4 to see whether a conflicting commit is prevented in every branch.
After that, decide whether the quorum arithmetic warrants an obligation or whether the Accept majority already covers even N.

feedback.answered: The even-N quorum question is grounded but unresolved at the run boundary: the code accepts even N, the recovery threshold is below a majority there, and the conflicting-recovery precondition was narrowed to a replica that reached the instance without recording its Commit, which is a membership/liveness condition rather than a quorum-size consequence.
